citation: Historic American Buildings Survey. John J. Glessner House, 1800 S. Prairie Avenue, Chicago, Cook County, Illinois. HABS IL-1015 (HABS ILL,16-CHIG,17-), measured drawings, sheets 1-6: sheet 1 title sheet with neighborhood plan (1" = 100', buildings from Bromley 1892), sheet 2 first floor plan (3/32" = 1'-0", del. Robert C. Giebner, June 1963), sheet 3 second floor plan (3/32" = 1'-0", del. Giebner), sheet 4 Section A-A (1/4" = 1'-0", del. Janis J. Erins), sheet 5 masonry details (1/4" = 1'-0", del. David T. Van Zanten), sheet 6 front (east) elevation (photogrammetric, photographed April 6, 1965, plotted at the Ohio State University under Perry E. Borchers, drawn by Eric N. DeLony). Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
author: Historic American Buildings Survey (H.A.B.S. Chicago Project 1963; sheet 6 prepared at the Ohio State University School of Architecture and Landscape Architecture)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division (HABS/HAER/HALS collection), item il0118; the six sheets are committed in this repository as chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/public/glessner-habs-sheet-1..6.png (and .tif), checksums in chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/acquired-files.json
locator: Sheets 1-6 as numbered in each sheet's title block ('SHEET n OF 6 SHEETS'). Dimensions are quoted from the printed dimension strings; anything else was measured off the committed 400-dpi scans with each sheet's own printed scale bar (sheets 2-3: 37.2 px per foot; sheets 4-5: 99-101 px per foot; sheet 6: 75.8 px per foot horizontally and 73.9 px per foot vertically, the vertical figure fixed by the sheet's own 48.62 ft chimney annotation). Every value in docs/RESEARCH/glessner_house_1904.md names its sheet.
rights_note: Works of the U.S. Government (National Park Service, HABS). LOC rights advisory for the collection: 'No known restrictions on images made by the U.S. Government; images copied from other sources may be restricted.' The measured drawings are HABS's own work, not copies.
access_notes: Read 2026-09-28 from the scans committed in chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/public/ (retrieved by the Prairie library under T-1633). The LOC item endpoints answered 403 to this session's unattended client, so nothing here was re-fetched.
note: A 1963-1965 survey of a building finished in December 1887. It measures the fabric itself, so it is the best dimensional evidence there is for the exterior, but it is not a 1904 witness: every value taken from it for a 1904 model has to clear the alterations the survey's own data pages list (habs_glessner_house_il_1015_data_pages, p. 3: September 1946 conversion) and, where it can, the 1888 photograph (inland_architect_1888_02_glessner_exterior). Sheet 2 itself flags two post-period items: 'WOODEN STAIRS BEHIND SERVICE WING ADDED C. 1955' and dotted stall partitions that are 'PROBABLE ... BASED ON EARLY DRAWINGS', not surveyed. Sheet 6 heights are referred to a local datum, '0.00 AT DOOR' (the Prairie Avenue front door sill), with the sidewalk before the doorway at -0.74; they are not Chicago City Datum. Section A-A (sheet 4) has no printed heights: its heights are measured off the drawing and referred to the grade it draws at the 18th Street wall.
what_it_supplies: the plan envelope of the house: 161'-3" along E. 18th Street, 74'-0" along Prairie Avenue, the 26'-6" east wing, the 35'-6" by 59'-9" west (stable) wing, the 26'-10" north range and the 47'-2" / 99'-3" courtyard (sheets 2-3 dimension strings)
courtyard-side projections: the round stair tower, the 9'-6" radius hall bow and the dining-room bay (sheet 2)
the east (Prairie Avenue) facade opening by opening, and its heights: 24.30 ft to the second-floor window soffits and 48.62 ft to the top of the north chimney above the door sill (sheet 6)
floor levels, eave and ridge heights and the roof profile of the north range, and the dormers, tower and eave of the east wing's courtyard slope (sheet 4)
the 18th Street entrance arch, the 18th Street carriage doorway, the Prairie Avenue entrance and the granite coursing (sheet 5)
the street-face openings of the north and west walls at first- and second-floor level, as gaps in the plans (sheets 2-3)
what_it_does_not_supply: a north (18th Street), west (alley) or courtyard elevation: none of the six sheets draws one, so heights on those faces come from sheets 4-5 and the 1888 photograph or are reconstructed
a roof plan: the E-W extent of the pyramid-roofed element in Section A-A, the stable roof and the roofs over the bays are not drawn
anything about 1904 as such: it is a 1963-1965 record
the colour of any material, or door and window hardware beyond what sheets 5-6 draw
lot lines: no sheet draws the property boundary except the thin south boundary wall on sheets 2-3
